mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active whenever the rate has declined over the past 3 months, and the direction of the return is positive regardless of the magnitude of the decline.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 3 months are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to expectations of monetary policy support and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods where UNRATE rises above 5.5% are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint condition of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 2.5%) signals a 'stagflation' regime, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to the market's anticipation of policy inaction and economic stagnation.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods meeting the stagflation condition are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low GDP growth (measured as the quarterly year-over-year change in GDPC1 below 1.0%), the S&P 500 is expected to produce positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to the anticipation of monetary policy support and the market's focus on the 'safe haven' effect of equities during economic slowdowns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where GDPC1 quarterly YoY change is below 1.0% are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month increase in the CPI index above 2.5% (annualized inflation rate) signals persistent inflation, leading to expectations of monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods where CPIAUCSL 12-month change exceeds 2.5% are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
